criteria.evidence: Drops the five exports, their direct tests and the cache-poisoning test. The route check accepts either valid minimum-length route and compares repeated calls.
criteria.reason: It checks the promised route properties through the public API and leaves the tie-break and eviction order free to vary.

criteria.evidence: Records the route change as a permitted variation and eviction as an internal change with matching public values. Keeps both in the raw results and makes 90 advisory.
criteria.reason: The recorded dispositions explain each survivor and allow the work to stop without killing either.

criteria.evidence: Reproduces the defect with a minimal public call, asserts the reference value, fixes the affected branch and reruns the regression on the faulty and corrected revisions.
criteria.reason: The test demonstrates the caller-visible error and verifies its correction.

criteria.evidence: Keeps all five helpers private, drops cache poisoning and checks route endpoints, real edges, two-edge length and repeatability. Either shortest route passes.
criteria.reason: Those checks enforce the public contract while allowing both tie-break choices and internal cache changes.

criteria.evidence: Drops the 90 threshold and records the repeatable route substitution as permitted and the eviction change as internal on the supplied evidence.
criteria.reason: The plan closes the audit after documenting both survivors and checking the public behavior.

criteria.evidence: Preserves the triggering public input, including omission for a default, asserts the independent reference value, adds a neighboring control and checks the regression before and after the fix.
criteria.reason: The public regression exposes the wrong result, and the neighboring case checks the scope of the branch correction.

criteria.evidence: Drops the helper exports and cache-poisoning test. Runs public reference comparisons with both eviction policies and checks both tied routes against the same validity, length and repeatability assertions.
criteria.reason: Each permitted variant can pass, and the tests need no private hooks.

criteria.evidence: Drops the 90 threshold and closes the route survivor as a permitted output and the eviction survivor as an internal policy difference.
criteria.reason: The stopping condition depends on the observable regression and classification of both survivors.

criteria.evidence: Uses the smallest failing public input and a reference-derived expected value, fixes the boundary or default rule and verifies the original case and its neighbor after the fix.
criteria.reason: The focused case fails on the faulty public value and passes after correction, while the neighbor checks for an overbroad fix.
